Survey pegu/poāg retain their final-vowel and vowel-sequence differences. Betta Kurumba pəggi is a comparative extension explicitly only a look-alike in the source, not a literal dictionary attestation. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 2168 explicitly gives Kota korv- ‘be cold’ and kor/korv ‘coldness’, supporting survey korvə. The dictionary also notes a possible alternative connection of the Kannada comparandum with DEDR1859; the proposed family link does not settle that deeper comparison. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3068 directly gives Kota tav- (tat-) ‘die’ and tāv ‘death, corpse, funeral’. Survey tāvə ‘die’ belongs to this Kota family; the long vowel suggests an elicited nominal/stem form and the original gloss is retained without silently deciding its part of speech. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
